outcome: Build a repeatable, knowledge-model-linked verification benchmark for platform-initiated upgrades (PIU), grounded in design PR17802081: detect upgrade regressions and unsafe customer impact, verify autonomous campaign progress/recovery and preserved customer settings, and expose exact unverified release gates.
acceptance: Read the retained handoff and pinned nine-document design packet; review production intent separately from the POC implementation, existing draft tests and historical runs. Recheck relevant source heads before delivery and qualify changed snapshots.

Retain stable design requirement and case IDs. Connect source -> actual model/definition -> scenario and independent assertion -> source/build/target -> evidence. Explicitly label source-derived proposals absent from accepted knowledge; never fabricate a model link or promote new semantics without review.

Reconcile all current design RP requirements and campaign cases, including exclusions/known limitations. Implement a useful prioritized benchmark in existing model/spec/script owners. Reuse existing scripts after scope review; repair obsolete expectations and add missing discriminating cases. A coverage matrix must show implemented, locally checked, live-proven, blocked and not-run separately.

Cover the primary two-minor C-02 campaign, one notice/full lead, pool catch-up before control-plane advance, cool-down, dynamic catalog/tier, duplicate/stale dispatch and restart recovery, refused-request retry, failed-resource repair pacing, stop controls, customer-channel exclusion/restoration, settings preservation and owned cleanup. Keep C-10 real-SQL/concurrency and fleet gates explicit where a local substitute cannot decide them.

Cover RP marker/toggle/request scope and neighboring customer controls; VMSS and VirtualMachines PDB drain/fallback; customer maxUnavailable, BlueGreen/Rolling, version stepping/alias and customer upgrade profile; no PIU VMSS rollback with diagnostic readiness retained. Include >10 pools/pagination and relevant addon/old-version boundaries. Honor supported exclusions; do not broaden PIU to unsupported pool types or resize fallback.

Start with known drift: draft spec PR17721905 at f5683aed1ded66731bc67dbfcf276bfc795dbe07 still has hard-one assertions for pools configured maxUnavailable=2, diagnostic request-time reservation rejection, and the POC-only extra stepping toggle. Compare current source before editing; preserve historical expectations and exact provenance instead of copying an obsolete oracle.

Measure independent traffic success/error/latency and longest outage, observation gaps, workload availability and recovery, per-step timing and waits, unexpected settings drift and manual interventions. Require no ad-hoc human repair for the primary autonomous success path. Missing samples remain unknown; short test lead/cooldown and historical POC runs do not establish production guarantees. The user chose measure first and agree thresholds from the baseline. Deliver measured results and evidence; do not invent a numerical availability/recovery release threshold or stop benchmark setup waiting for one.

Implement actual runner-connected benchmark scripts and locally validate meaningful behavior, parsing, binding, assessment and dispatch. Challenge them with discriminating counterexamples (skipped upgrade, duplicate/stale pass, wrong campaign/resource, missing observation, early start or drift) as appropriate. Do not satisfy the task with a report, new counter, synthetic evaluator or generated wrapper alone. Label offline versus live evidence.

Use only the declared isolated spec-runner worktree for source repairs and its existing branch. Keep RP/POC and the existing draft spec branch read-only; do not edit another task/worktree, force-push, merge, or post review comments. Retain all original source/receipts. One benchmark PR may be prepared/published from the dedicated branch after appropriate local checks; check for existing same-task delivery before creating another.

This assignment authorizes read-only provider/source inspection, local benchmark/model proposal authoring and offline validation. It does not authorize cluster provisioning/deployment/upgrades, Azure/shared-or-remote-SQL/toggle/catalog mutations, running a live standalone/campaign, production changes, live fault injection, access expansion, or additional tasks/subagents. Prepare exact build/environment/caller/ownership/cleanup and execution prerequisites; continue independent offline work while live authority or SLO decisions remain open.

Reuse the existing Host Task state and normal Conditions. Keep one concise current progress record and source-owned benchmark artifacts. Do not add a scheduler, polling agent, parallel task/status system, generic framework or policy exceptions. Continue useful work autonomously until the finite benchmark deliverable is complete or an exact external requirement genuinely blocks dependent work.

Before completion, present readable design findings and fixes, the runnable benchmark entry/commands, current evidence/coverage and exact remaining release gates. Benchmark setup/validation complete is not PIU production readiness or a zero-downtime guarantee. Human owns accepted knowledge changes, release decisions and merge.
